content.thinking: No /usr/bin/time. Let me use Python's resource module or a wrapper to measure. I'll write a small measuring runner using subprocess + resource.getrusage(RUSAGE_CHILDREN).

arguments.command:
cat > /workspace/dev/bench.py << 'PYEOF'
import resource, subprocess, sys, time, os
prog = '/workspace/submission/scheduler.py'
for name in sys.argv[1:]:
    inp = '/workspace/tmp/big_%s.json' % name
    before = resource.getrusage(resource.RUSAGE_CHILDREN)
    t0 = time.time()
    with open(inp, 'rb') as f, open('/workspace/tmp/out_%s.json' % name, 'wb') as o:
        p = subprocess.run([sys.executable, '-I', '-B', prog], stdin=f, stdout=o,
                           stderr=subprocess.PIPE)
    t1 = time.time()
    after = resource.getrusage(resource.RUSAGE_CHILDREN)
    cpu = (after.ru_utime - before.ru_utime) + (after.ru_stime - before.ru_stime)
    print('%-8s rc=%d wall=%.2fs cpu=%.2fs maxrss=%dMB outsize=%d'
          % (name, p.returncode, t1 - t0, cpu,
             after.ru_maxrss // 1024, os.path.getsize('/workspace/tmp/out_%s.json' % name)))
    if p.returncode != 0:
        print('   stderr:', p.stderr[:400])
PYEOF
cd /workspace && python3 dev/bench.py stream stream2 burst burst2 burst3
